projects.title: Helios Dynamics
projects.description: A solar-grade identity system forged for a private space-launch venture.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.content: Helios Aerospace approached us to forge an identity worthy of the next era of orbital flight — a system that could feel both engineered and human across launch livery, mission control, and the screens of millions watching from the ground.

sections.heading: The Challenge
sections.content: The brand had grown through a decade of acquisitions, leaving a fractured visual language with no single voice. Every spacecraft, deck, and microsite spoke differently, and the gap between the engineering culture and the public story had widened into something unmissable.

sections.heading: The Solution
sections.content: We built a precise, modular identity around a single radiant mark and a monolithic typographic system. Motion principles, a calibrated dark palette, and a flexible grid let the brand scale from a 3-second launch sting to a 300-page technical manual without ever losing its center of gravity.

projects.title: Orbital
projects.description: An immersive WebGL product story for an orbital-logistics platform.

sections.heading: The Challenge
sections.content: The product was abstract and invisible: data moving between objects we will never see. Communicating that with clarity, without drowning the story in jargon or hollow 3D spectacle, demanded restraint as much as ambition.

sections.heading: The Solution
sections.content: We designed a cinematic, scroll-choreographed journey anchored by a live constellation visualization. Each section reveals one layer of the system, pacing the technical depth so a five-minute read feels like a guided flight rather than a datasheet.

projects.title: Nocturne
projects.description: Title design and a motion language for a nocturnal sound label.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.content: Nocturne Audio builds reference-grade listening hardware for people who treat sound as architecture. We were asked to direct the launch film and motion system for their first flagship product.

sections.heading: The Challenge
sections.content: Audio is the hardest thing to show. We needed to make stillness feel charged — to translate the experience of a perfectly quiet room and a single resolving note into something a viewer could feel in under ninety seconds.

sections.heading: The Solution
sections.content: We shot a sequence built almost entirely on negative space, light, and micro-movement, then scored the edit to the product’s own frequency response. The motion language carried into the site and store, so the campaign felt like one continuous breath.

projects.title: Meridian
projects.description: A real-time spatial interface for a deep-sensing research lab.

sections.heading: The Challenge
sections.content: Real-time WebGL at this fidelity fights against performance, accessibility, and the simple human need to not get lost. The interface had to feel weightless on a laptop while rendering millions of points without ever stuttering or disorienting.

sections.heading: The Solution
sections.content: We built a custom navigation grammar and a layered level-of-detail system that loads the world as you move through it. Considered lighting, a muted palette, and clear spatial cues keep the focus on understanding the space rather than fighting the controls.

projects.title: Eclipse
projects.description: The darkest luxury brand world, built entirely in shadow.

sections.heading: The Challenge
sections.content: Going this dark is a liability in retail and in e-commerce alike — black on black reads as a void or a defect unless every edge, finish, and shadow is deliberate. The brand needed depth without ever feeling like an error.

sections.heading: The Solution
sections.content: We engineered a system of near-black surfaces separated only by texture, foil, and the faintest specular highlight. Packaging, type, and the digital storefront share one obsessive rule: light is the only color, and it is rationed with intent.

projects.title: Pale Blue
projects.description: A climate non-profit's data-driven story of a fragile planet.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.content: The Pale Blue Foundation funds climate and ocean research. They needed a digital home that could hold rigorous science and genuine emotion in the same frame, and move people from reading to giving.

sections.heading: The Challenge
sections.content: Nonprofit sites tend to drift into either dry data or empty sentiment. The challenge was to honor the research with real depth while keeping the experience human enough that a first-time visitor would stay, feel something, and act.

sections.heading: The Solution
sections.content: We structured the site around a single descending narrative — from the scale of the planet down to one fundable project — paired with a calm, data-forward visual system. Clear giving moments are woven through the story rather than bolted onto the end.
